title: Feature request: "Yes, but..." during permissions prompts
body:
I frequently find myself in a situation where Claude proposes a file edit or a command execution that is very, very close to what I want it to do. So close, in fact, that I'd rather it execute that change and then take some direction from me to make a targeted follow-up change.  

Right now, my options are:

Yes. Do it.
Yes. And just keep going without checking in.
No. Don't do it. Stop.

I'd really love a fourth option:

*Yes. But then stop for a prompt.*

I can work around this by hitting "Yes. Do it" and then hitting escape once Claude has started in on its next thing, but that often ends up with polluted context and feels clunky.
author: obra
